item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"The fragment structures should be interpreted as incomplete views of the syntaxin N-terminal domain, not as fold-defining examples of independent domains. In SCOPe’s current view, 1br0 and 1ez3 are syntaxin N-terminal-domain fragments whose helices can support only a local annotation, while 1dn1 chain B supplies the intact syntaxin domain context and is the appropriate structure for assigning the full all-alpha syntaxin N-terminal-domain fold. The practical consequence is that a hit to 1br0 or 1ez3 is evidence for the corresponding syntaxin helical fragment, not enough by itself to transfer the complete family/superfamily/fold, whole-domain boundaries, or representative status; full-domain homology and template choice should be based on the 1dn1B-like complete domain rather than on those early partial NMR fragments alone.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
